questions.stem: Choose the word that is most nearly the SAME in meaning to the given word: OBFUSCATE
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: 'Obfuscate' means to deliberately make something unclear, obscure, or difficult to understand. 'Confuse' is the exact synonym. Example: Politicians often use complex legal jargon to obfuscate the truth.
DECOY BUSTING: 'Clarify', 'Illuminate', and 'Simplify' are all exact antonyms (opposites) of Obfuscate.
EXAM INSIGHT: Vocabulary questions often present three antonyms and one synonym. If you don't know the target word but notice three options mean the exact same thing (clarify/illuminate/simplify), the odd one out is usually the answer.

questions.stem: Choose the word that is most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to the given word: GREGARIOUS
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: 'Gregarious' describes a person who is fond of company, highly sociable, and outgoing (derived from the Latin word 'grex' meaning 'flock'). The opposite is 'Introverted', meaning someone who prefers to be alone or is shy.
DECOY BUSTING: 'Sociable', 'Outgoing', and 'Talkative' are all synonyms of Gregarious.
EXAM INSIGHT: Always double-check if the question asks for a synonym or antonym. In exam pressure, students often pick the synonym (Sociable) by mistake because their brain immediately recognizes the association.

questions.stem: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom: 'To spill the beans'

options.option_text: To drop your food on the floor
To work very hard on a farm
To completely ruin a plan intentionally

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: 'To spill the beans' means to leak a secret, either accidentally or prematurely. For example, "We were planning a surprise party for John, but Sarah spilled the beans."
DECOY BUSTING: Idioms rarely mean their literal interpretation (dropping food). 'Ruining a plan' is similar but lacks the specific context of revealing hidden information.
EXAM INSIGHT: A similar idiom is 'To let the cat out of the bag', which also means revealing a secret.
